nodes.summary: Let $C_m$ be the Clausen-type function of Entry 13, with $C_0 = 0$ and $C_1(x) = -\log\lvert 2\sin(x/2)\rvert$. For every natural number $m \ge 2$ and every real $x$, $C_m(x) = \sum_{k \ge 1} \sin(kx)/k^m$ if $m$ is even and $C_m(x) = \sum_{k \ge 1} \cos(kx)/k^m$ if $m$ is odd.
nodes.title: Clausen functions of order at least two as series (Chapter 9, Entry 13)

nodes.summary: The order-one Clausen-type function $C_1$ of Entry 13 is the log-sine function: for every real $x$, $C_1(x) = -\log\lvert 2\sin(x/2)\rvert$, with the convention $\log 0 = 0$, so that $C_1$ vanishes at the integer multiples of $2\pi$.
nodes.title: Clausen function of order one (Chapter 9, Entry 13)

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $m$ and $k$ and a real number $x$, let $t_k = \sin((k+1)x)/(k+1)^m$ if $m$ is even and $t_k = \cos((k+1)x)/(k+1)^m$ if $m$ is odd. Then $\lvert t_k\rvert \le 1/(k+1)^m$.
nodes.title: Termwise bound for the Clausen series (Chapter 9, Entry 13)

nodes.summary: For every natural number $m \ge 2$ and every real $x$, the series $\sum_{k \ge 1} \sin(kx)/k^m$ (if $m$ is even) or $\sum_{k \ge 1} \cos(kx)/k^m$ (if $m$ is odd) is summable.
nodes.title: Summability of the Clausen series (Chapter 9, Entry 13)

nodes.summary: The Clausen-type functions $C_m$ of Entry 13 are defined by $C_1(x) = -\log\lvert 2\sin(x/2)\rvert$ and, for $m \ge 2$, $C_m(x) = \sum_{k \ge 1} \sin(kx)/k^m$ for even $m$ and $C_m(x) = \sum_{k \ge 1} \cos(kx)/k^m$ for odd $m$, together with the convention $C_0 = 0$: for every real $x$, $C_0(x) = 0$.
nodes.title: Clausen function of order zero (Chapter 9, Entry 13)

nodes.summary: Let $m \ge 2$ be an integer, and let $s_m = \sin$ if $m$ is even and $s_m = \cos$ if $m$ is odd. For real $x$ write $C_m(x) = \sum_{k \ge 1} s_m(kx)/k^m$ and $O_m(x) = \sum_{k \ge 0} s_m((2k+1)x)/(2k+1)^m$. Then for every real $x$, $O_m(x) = C_m(x) - 2^{-m} C_m(2x)$.
nodes.title: Odd-frequency part of a Clausen series for $m \ge 2$

nodes.summary: For real $x$ let $C_1(x) = -\log|2 \sin(x/2)|$ and $O_1(x) = -\tfrac{1}{2} \log|\tan(x/2)|$. For an integer $m \ge 2$, let $s_m = \sin$ if $m$ is even and $s_m = \cos$ if $m$ is odd, and let $C_m(x) = \sum_{k \ge 1} s_m(kx)/k^m$ and $O_m(x) = \sum_{k \ge 0} s_m((2k+1)x)/(2k+1)^m$. Then for every integer $m \ge 1$ and every real $x$ with $x \ne 0$ and $|x| < \pi$, $O_m(x) = C_m(x) - 2^{-m} C_m(2x)$.
nodes.title: Odd-frequency part of a Clausen function for $0 < |x| < \pi$

nodes.summary: For an integer $m \ge 0$ let $s_m = \sin$ if $m$ is even and $s_m = \cos$ if $m$ is odd. For real $x$, the odd Clausen function $O_m(x)$ is $0$ if $m = 0$, is $-\tfrac{1}{2} \log|\tan(x/2)|$ if $m = 1$, and is otherwise given by a series: for every integer $m \ge 2$ and every real $x$, $O_m(x) = \sum_{k \ge 0} s_m((2k+1)x)/(2k+1)^m$.
nodes.title: The odd Clausen function as a series for $m \ge 2$

nodes.summary: For an integer $m \ge 0$ let $s_m = \sin$ if $m$ is even and $s_m = \cos$ if $m$ is odd. The odd Clausen functions $O_m$, for integers $m \ge 0$, are given by $O_0 = 0$, by $O_m(x) = \sum_{k \ge 0} s_m((2k+1)x)/(2k+1)^m$ for $m \ge 2$, and at $m = 1$ by a closed form: for every real $x$, $O_1(x) = -\tfrac{1}{2} \log|\tan(x/2)|$.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
